transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Um, well, I'm a receptionist at a hotel, and lately... I've just been really on edge. What really pushed me to make this appointment is that, well, every time a door slams at work, or even if someone just rolls a suitcase really fast across the lobby floor, I just... I jump. Like, really jump, like it's happening all over again. And then my heart is just racing, and it takes me a good minute or so just to get it back down to normal. It's just getting really hard to deal with.
When you say it feels like it's happening all over again, is there a specific past event or experience that comes to mind in those moments?

Yeah, it's... well, this has been going on for about two weeks now. It started right after this incident at the front desk where a guest got really aggressive and, um, actually threatened me. So whenever I hear those loud noises now, my mind just goes right back to that moment.
Do these episodes of your heart racing and feeling on edge ever happen suddenly, out of nowhere, when there's no loud noise or reminder of the incident at all?

Yeah, actually, it does. Um, sometimes out of nowhere, I’ll just get this picture in my head of that guest leaning over the counter and knocking the front desk equipment toward me. It doesn't even take a loud noise to trigger it. I could just be trying to answer a normal phone call, and suddenly that image is just there, and I feel on edge all over again.
Have you found yourself avoiding certain situations, people, or places at work—like avoiding the front desk area or certain guests—because they remind you of that incident?

Yeah, I have. Um, I've actually started taking the back hallway whenever I can. Walking past the exact spot in the lobby where it happened... it just makes my chest tighten up. I just really want to stay away from that area.
Since the incident, have you noticed times when you feel detached from yourself or your surroundings—like you're in a daze, things feel unreal, or you're watching yourself from outside your body?

Yeah, I have noticed that a little bit. Um, sometimes when I have to be back near the front desk, the whole lobby just feels kind of distant and unreal for a few seconds. It's a weird feeling, like... like I'm watching myself work instead of actually being fully there in the moment.
